patch.objective: Security alerting and monitoring: monitoring systems, applications, and infrastructure; log aggregation, alerting, scanning, reporting, archiving, and alert response and remediation/validation (quarantine, alert tuning); tools (Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP), benchmarks, agents/agentless, SIEM, antivirus, data loss prevention (DLP), SNMP traps, NetFlow, vulnerability scanners)
secondaryObjectives: Incident response activities as SY0-701 names them: preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned; training; testing (tabletop exercise, simulation); root cause analysis; threat hunting; digital forensics (legal hold, chain of custody, acquisition, reporting, preservation, e-discovery)

sources.cite: CompTIA Security+ (V7), exam SY0-701: domains General security concepts 12%, Threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigations 22%, Security architecture 18%, Security operations 28%, Security program management and oversight 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 for this Security+ band of a CySA+ incident. Relevant text (Security operations): 'Vulnerability management: identifying, analyzing, remediating, validating, and reporting vulnerabilities'; 'Alerting and monitoring: explaining monitoring tools and computing resource activities.' The objectives PDF was not re-read; the objective titles are the course seed's.

sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Exam Objectives Document Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23; domains 34/26/24/16)
sources.note: Relevant text: 1.2 'Given a scenario, analyze indicators of potential malicious activity' (host-related indicators: resource consumption, unauthorized software, anomalous activity: suspicious or rogue processes, Living Off the Land Binaries (LOLBins) and Scripts, file system changes, data exfiltration); 2.3 'Given a scenario, analyze data to prioritize and mitigate vulnerabilities' (exploitability, active exploitation/threat intelligence, asset value, impact, patch/remediation availability, true/false positives, true/false negatives; CVSS metrics, EPSS); 3.2 'Summarize the incident response process' (containment, recovery); 3.3 'Given a scenario, implement incident response techniques' (triage, establishment of a timeline, determining severity and impact, escalation; isolating affected targets, remediation and verification, release from isolation, performing restoration). Read in the official objectives PDF (the course's officialObjectivesUrl) through a summarizing fetch, and the CompTIA V4 page, on 2026-11-11. CS0-003 retires for English on 2026-12-22.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile (April 2025)
sources.note: The current revision (April 3, 2025; supersedes Rev. 2 of 2012). Relevant text: RS.MA-02 'Perform a preliminary review of a new incident report to verify that a cybersecurity incident has occurred, then estimate the severity of the incident and the level of urgency'; RS.MA-03 'Prioritize how quickly incident response should be performed for each incident based on its scope, likely impact, time-critical nature, and resource availability'; RS.MA-04 escalation and elevation; RS.MI-01 'Containment refers to preventing the expansion of an incident'; RS.MI-02 eradication 'to eliminate persistence mechanisms and entry points' and 'Identify all affected hosts and services'; RS.AN-07 incident data collected with integrity and provenance preserved; RS.CO-02 stakeholders notified. Read in the PDF text (nvlpubs.nist.gov) and the CSRC page on 2026-11-11.
